newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran military may discharge corruption critic.
newsitem.headline: Honduran military may discharge corruption critic.

text.p: An officer who denounced corruption in Honduras' armed forces will be brought before a military tribunal where he was expected to receive a dishonourable discharge, the nation's top military official said on Wednesday.
Col. Guadalupe Reythel Caballero denounced what he called "illicit enrichement" in the upper echelons of the armed forces.
The charges, contained in an internal military document known as "Informe R" that was leaked to the local press, shook a military hierarchy that had long been used to impunity for any wrongdoings.
"I am not the one who will give the dishonourable discharge, rather the respective tribunal will apply the law," said Gen. Mario Hung, chief of the armed forces.

"If there is an officer who commits a fault, it is my duty to bring him before the respective court and apply the required laws," Hung told a news conference after a meeting of the military's highest council.
Reythel's lawyer, Pablo Valladares, said if the military sacked his client he would take the case to other courts in Honduras and abroad.
"They are violating his rights only because he told the truth. What he wrote is true, and I am going to ask for an investigation of many of the officers who got rich overnight," Valladares said.
The colonel was confined to his home and gained the protection of the government's National Commission for the Protection of Human Rights.

Honduras' military, supported heavily by the United States during the conflictive years of the 1980s in Central America, runs a wide range of businesses and has a strong influence on the civilian government.
The military's Hung said if someone is going to bring charges of corruption, they should first present proof.
